concept.name: Support
concept.definition: A price level or zone at which demand is thought to be strong enough to prevent the price from declining further. It is a core hypothesis of technical analysis about where buying interest concentrates, not a guaranteed floor.
concept.intuition: As price gets cheaper, buyers become more willing to buy and sellers less willing to sell, so declines tend to pause there.
concept.mechanics: Commonly established at previous reaction lows, broken resistance levels (polarity), round numbers, or moving averages. Because TA is not an exact science, practitioners often mark support as a zone rather than an exact price; a decisive break below is read as supply overcoming demand.
concept.failure_modes: Support breaks happen regularly, especially in high volatility or around news; once broken, the old level can invert into resistance, trapping buyers who assumed it would hold.
concept.misconceptions: That support is a precise price that must hold; brief dips below a level are common and do not necessarily invalidate it.
concept.example: ChartSchool cites Halliburton returning repeatedly to support in the low 30s (October 1999 low near 31, December near 33, February near 32.5) before the level was tested again.
